title: Effects of Harvest and Fertilization Frequency on Protein Yield and Extractability from Flood-Tolerant Perennial Grasses Cultivated on a Fen Peatland
license: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY), as stated in the article
units: CNCPS fraction concentrations in g/kg dry matter; fraction share as percent of total crude protein. SD is provided for concentration only; the article's table does not give SD for share percentages.
transformation: Annual-average concentration means and parenthetical SDs transcribed into numeric columns. Published share percentages transcribed as integer percent. No conversion, interpolation, or recalculation.

definitions.B1+B2: Neutral-detergent soluble crude-protein fractions as defined by the CNCPS method in the article.
definitions.B1+B2+B3: Potentially extractable protein fraction including acid-detergent soluble B3; a theoretical fraction, not measured recovered product.

applicability: Harvest-regime-dependent protein fraction reference for cultivated reed canary grass and tall fescue; not a GreenHub roadside-grass measurement or extraction efficiency.
limitations: CNCPS fraction concentrations are not equivalent to screw-press release, acid-precipitation recovery, or product yield.
The two species were cultivated on Danish fen peatland; they are not mixed roadside grass.
Fertilizer N/K regime differed between one-cut and 2–5-cut treatments, confounding treatment comparisons.
The study states raw data can be requested from authors; this extract contains only published table values.
